chapter: Pianists, the district and Stormy Weather
title: Sheet music, a pianist who read music, and Dr. Blanks
summary: Who has old sheet music; a piano player who couldn't play without music; his brother-in-law Dr. Herbert Blanks and a hard baby grand piano.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Did you have any old sheet music? You know anybody who has any old sheet music?
Well, Paul, boy, yeah. You know he had plenty of music.
Yeah, I know.

George had plenty of music. Which George? George Gannon. Oh, yeah. He wrote Beethoven. See one of them fellas guys that people take that stuff and burn it all up, you know? Yeah, they don't care. They don't care. They don't think about that.
Yeah, well Paul's old. His wife was dead, I think.
Yeah, he was old with me. He died. He stole everything in his house. They did?
Yeah.
He didn't steal the candle. He couldn't get the candle. He couldn't move it.
Well, when did they get in to steal something?

Oh, they break him. They were breaking your house, man. After he died? Yeah, after he died. He broke his house. Because my brother was living right around the corner of him. And Leroy was living right across the street from him. Leroy still lives across the street from him. He lived on John Mill, Robinson Street between Govary Nichols and Glacelon. He was a good piano player. He was a good piano player. He couldn't play no jazz. He couldn't play no jazz. Like I say, we ever heard, I say, well, I'm not a jazz.
Never have heard of him. I know him. I know him. I know him on the phone.
He was a piano player. Read music like upside down. Good piano player.
What did he do when the lights went out?
I don't know what he did. The lights, they made sure that the lights didn't go out.
Yeah, I see. But he couldn't play anything without the music.
Couldn't play nothing. Because my sister-in-law had a big grand piano. Her husband broke up. But she had a big grand piano. We used to go down there all night. He went to Dr. Blanks.
I was going to ask you about him. Who is Dr. Blanks?

That's the band you used to sing with. White Tails. He used to sing in White Tails. Is his right name Dr. Blanks? No, his name was Herbert Blanks. Herbert Blanks? And he married my sister. He's got a $30,000 home now in the basin. What a little country town's out there. Bay St. Louis. What a little town.
Is he a medical doctor?

He's a dentist. Oh, a dentist. A dentist doctor. He come out of Cairo, Illinois. Dr. Blanks. I used to count these mothers. $154 a day. Pulling teeth. When he had them soldiers, you know, contract with the government. You know, pulling them soldiers teeth. And he bought a baby grand piano. He put it down there. Nice to go down there and practice on the team. But I ain't never seen a piano so hard to play in my whole life. Is that baby grand piano. All you know, I have to bail down on the keys and all that kind of stuff. I have no nice, easy, boring piano. You know, like my sister-in-law. My sister-in-law got a... She got a... Sixteen... Sixteen... She got a tree of... She called them things. You know, she called them... She called them... She's a little piano about that big. Spin it? I don't spin it, yeah. That nice little piano. She's still so far out there, I can't get that. I got a job to play with the name of the whole company. Play with the band, you know.
